newsitem.title: USA: Andrews to buy Toy Biz for $22.50/shr.
newsitem.headline: Andrews to buy Toy Biz for $22.50/shr.

text.p: Andrews Group Inc said on Friday it signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire all class A shares of Toy Biz Inc common stock held by Toy Biz public stockholders for $22.50 per share.
But Andrews said the deal would depend on Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's plan of reorganization filed on Friday with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the district of Delaware.

As part of Marvel's plan for reorganization, Andrews Group said it would acquire from Marvel for $365 million in cash or Toy Biz Class A common stock or a combination of these, newly issued shares of Marvel common stock representing 80.8 percent of the outstanding shares of Marvel common stock after giving effect to the acquisition.
In effect, Andrews was making an equity investment in Marvel Entertainment in exchange for newly issued shares.
Financier Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group controls Marvel Entertainment and owns about 80 million shares.
Andrews said on December 16 a special committee of Toy Biz's board endorsed a proposed transaction under which Andrews would buy Toy Biz Class A common shares owned by shareholders for $22.50 each.

On November 20, Andrews agreed to buy the 67 percent of Toy Biz shares held by Isaac Perlmutter and Avi Arad for about $17 per share. At that time, it also proposed buying remaing Toy Biz Class A shares for $19 per share.
But the Toy Biz board backed a transaction under which Andrews would purchase the remaining Class A shares for $22.50 per share, Andrews said.
Marvel owns all of the Toy Biz Class B shares, which equated to about 27 percent of Toy Biz Inc. A Marvel spokesman said Andrews was buying all Toy Biz shares not owned by Marvel for $365 million.

Marvel Entertainment said on Friday it filed a Chapter 11 petition to carry out a proposed $525 million recapitalization that would enable Marvel to pursue new strategic intiatives and achieve sustained profitability.
Marvel said the filing was necessitated by the failure of the holders of bonds issued by Marvel's holding companies to reach agreement regarding any alternative plans for the company's future.

In a separate release on Friday, Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdigns and Marvel III Holdings said they also filed voluntary peittions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in a Delaware court.
The three holding companies said they owned 80.2 million shares of Marvel Entertainment common stock.

If the reorganization plan was confirmed, Andrews said on Friday it expected to assign its rights and obligations under the Toy Biz merger agreement to Marvel and that Toy Biz would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Marvel.
